title: Throughput Reservation Railgun + Staged Rolling Upgrades for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Implement a two-part system that (1) reserves and carves out short-lived throughput lanes ('Railgun' reservations) to preserve SLOs during node drains/upgrades, and (2) drives a staged rolling upgrade workflow that minimizes tail-latency and KV-cache cold starts across Dedicated fleets. This ticket covers design, prototype, and alpha rollout for a single availability zone before cross-AZ rollout.

Background: We frequently see SLO regressions when maintenance and autoscaler churn converge — batch windows collapse and KV cache warms cause tokenized spikes. Existing drain flows are all-or-nothing and lack a cheap short-term reservation primitive to guarantee throughput for critical customer contracts.

High-level approach:
- Reservation primitive (Railgun): lightweight lease object that pins a fraction of capacity for a tenant or system-level SLO for a bounded time window (defaults: 60s, configurable). Reservations bypass best-effort eviction heuristics and are honored by the autoscaler and scheduler.
- Staged rolling upgrades: split host replacement into prepare (prewarm KV cache + load-simulated warmups), tranche drain (move non-reserved requests first), and sweep (evict remaining). Each tranche uses active telemetry to decide whether to proceed or pause.
- Autoscaler integration: when reservations are active, autoscaler emits a temporary soft-capacity increment (hedge nodes) to avoid breaking SLOs under bursty load.
- Observability: per-reservation metrics (reserved_tokens/sec, success_rate, average_latency), tranche timeline events, and recovery dashboards.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Reservation API available to internal controllers and rollout engine.
2) A rolling upgrade of 100 hosts with 10% reservation load shows <5% regression in p99 latency vs baseline and no customer-visible qps loss.
3) Autoscaler honors reservation signals and can create short-lived hedge nodes within configured SLA.
4) Dashboarding: reservations are visible with start/end, owner, and impact score.

Design trade-offs discussed:
- Reservation duration: shorter windows reduce resource waste but increase scheduling pressure; we choose a default 60s with exponential backoff retry.
- Soft vs hard reservations: prefer soft reservations with autoscaler hedging to avoid hard-capacity fragmentation in small fleets.
- Prewarm cost: prewarming KV caches costs tokens and scheduling time; we’ll provide a config knob per-customer for prewarm aggressiveness.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 1 (Prototype, 2 sprints): local reservation primitive, simple tranche state machine, unit+integration tests, design doc.
- Phase 2 (Alpha): autoscaler integration, basic prewarm hook, internal-only rollout on 2 test fleets, latency/burn charts.
- Phase 3 (Beta): policy knobs in Console, rollout controls for operators, dashboarding + QA.
- Phase 4: GA with customer opt-in and documented runbook.

Risks & mitigations:
- Over-reservation increasing cost: we implement per-customer caps and eviction policies.
- Scheduler complexity: start with scheduler advisory API and avoid making reservations mandatory for placement until proven.
- Edge-case deadlocks between autoscaler and reservation leases: leases auto-expire and the autoscaler treats stale leases as no-op after TTL.

2026-03-02 - Prototype PR opened: initial reservation object + scheduler advisory API. Awaiting review from Simone (infra). PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/11234

2026-03-05 - Load test: synthetic qps+tail test: 10k req/s for 5 min while performing 20 host drains. Observed p99 uplift 8% without Railgun; with prototype reservations uplift reduced to 2.5%. See dashboard for details.
2026-03-08 - Design review notes: Add autoscaler hedging, expose reservation visibility in Console. PM requests soft-cap defaults to avoid fragmentation.

2026-03-10 - Blocker: small race found between lease expiry and autoscaler snapshot leading to transient over-provision. Mitigation: extend lease_end by 2s in snapshot window and add idempotency token. Assigned to Eng:Simone.
